prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1057; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Claimant reports being struck while exiting a parking space by another vehicle. Claimant reports a wrist injury at the scene and has since been seen by a physician. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Initial contact made by phone; claimant cooperative and requested written correspondence.

Entry 2: Recorded statements obtained from both drivers. Claimant states the other vehicle backed out without checking for pedestrians or traffic. Other driver acknowledges reversing and states visibility was limited by a parked van. Photos of both vehicles received from claimant and show damage to the rear quarter panel of the claimant's vehicle and the front bumper of the other vehicle. No witnesses identified at this time.

Entry 3: Medical documentation received from claimant. Records indicate a fracture of the wrist with a splint applied and follow-up scheduled with an orthopedic specialist. Claimant advised of the general process for submitting medical bills and of the right to seek independent advice. Claimant stated she has not yet decided whether to consult an attorney.

Entry 4: Liability review in progress. Parking lot surveillance footage requested from the property owner; response pending. Preliminary assessment suggests the other driver bears primary responsibility for the collision based on the statements and damage pattern, though this remains subject to the footage review. Repair estimate for claimant's vehicle received and under review.

Entry 5: Follow-up call placed to claimant to confirm receipt of correspondence and update on the footage request. Claimant reports ongoing pain and limited grip strength and is awaiting the specialist appointment. Claimant asked about timing for a settlement decision; advised that the injury claim will remain open until treatment is complete and medical records are final. File flagged for supervisor review of the injury component.
